https://spacetimedb.com/docs/databases/transactions-atomicity/

The pinned v2.6.1 host maps a user error to `EventStatus::FailedUser` and sends

The subscription actor rolls back the mutable transaction for a failed user

https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/blob/v2.6.1/crates/core/src/subscription/module_subscription_actor.rs#L1604-L1643

Applied to the source-derived removal path in checkpoint 3081, the error rolls

# Applied splint custody follow-up

Pinned application source shows that `equip_splint` associates a quantity-one
personal inventory row with `LimbInjury.splint_inventory_item_id` and that
`return_splint` requires that exact row. The general
`inventory_item_is_equipped` guard checks `character_equipped_item` wearables,
not the injury table. The personal discard and party-deposit reducers use that
guard and do not visibly consult the splint association.

For a patient with an applied splint backed by an ordinary inventory row,
the discard path accepts the patient's row and deletes it. The injury keeps
its splint reference; later explicit removal or completed fracture healing
calls `return_splint` and errors because the referenced item is missing. The
party-deposit path can also remove the personal row while the injury refers to
it. This is source-derived, not runtime tested. The physical-object-backed
case and all other transfer paths require separate tracing.

The connected repair should prevent transfer, discard, sale, or other custody
changes of an applied splint except through a single authorized release path,
and preserve the exact item and rightful owner. Check lifecycle, character
death, and contained-object behavior before choosing the final contract.

The pinned item catalog defines splint as a simple item without equipment or
capabilities. The normal item projection defaults those fields, and
`requires_stable_object` does not require a stable object for this definition:
it is not food, measured material, repairable equipment, medication, a melee
weapon, a container, or an attachment-point provider. Thus ordinary grants
create stackable inventory rows without physical-object identities, supporting
the normal-row example above. This does not rule out exceptional creation
paths or malformed pre-existing object records.

For a hypothetical splint with an existing physical-object identity,

The death and estate path adds a distinct conditional lifecycle case. If the
splint's recorded owner dies while the item is applied to another patient, the
row is held in the patient's inventory and is not part of the owner's current

If a patient dies with another character's splint still applied, the estate

damage, not splint custody. This is a conditional source inference; intended

generic arbitrary short pause; a surviving patient may be left untreated when
the surgeon is the participant who reaches the boundary. Other lifecycle
interactions and any nonterminal clipping require independent qualification.

Lifecycle splitting does not itself stop a wait: relationship boundaries
divide it into segments, each of which settles age, continuity, billing,
weddings, births, courtship, marriage, and patient context. A recovered
outbreak patient's clock advancement can close their case membership at the
new minute. Case membership validity excludes its `left_at` endpoint; the
post-wait treatment check evaluates at the actor's advanced minute. If the
selected claim is no longer valid and no other matching membership applies,
the check returns unavailable and the reducer returns an error. The pinned
server rollback then undoes the wait and context release together. This is a
conditional source-derived scenario; verify clock ordering, visibility,
recovery boundaries, and normal reachability before asserting an end-to-end
failure or choosing the desired resolution. For distinct participants with
aligned clocks and an uninterrupted full wait, the actor is advanced first and
the patient second to the same ending minute. Closing membership records that
minute as `left_at` and increments its revision. At the following check the
closed membership is invalid at that endpoint; depending on remaining presence,
the preceding co-location check may fail first, or the supplied claim may be
unavailable. Either error reaches the reducer and rolls the transaction back.

Generated outbreak materialization creates case-site patient membership with
treatment decision `Allowed` and an open interval while a surviving patient is
before the course end. The guarded lifecycle fixture verifies an open patient
and later recovery cleanup, but it explicitly remediates the case first and
does not exercise treatment spanning recovery. Thus the producer supplies the
relevant permission and recovery state in principle; an open, visible patient
with an eligible wound and synchronized clocks still needs a complete supported
scenario. The fixture was inspected, not executed.

The typed `Allowed` reason distinguishes self-action, target permission, and
emergency necessity at decision construction. The core decision function
preserves explicit refusal and permits the emergency exception only for an
unavailable answer; the emergency predicate is restricted to an incapacitated
patient's open, unbandaged cut. Current surgery checks authorization before
and after waiting but matches `Allowed(_)` both times. The other searched
module consumers similarly use the allowed/refused/unavailable outcome rather
than inspecting the reason. No current downstream requirement to persist the
reason was found in these searched consumers; this does not by itself justify
removing the type or closing the broader consent contract.
